doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Resolving the Bela Fleck Hoedown copyright issue
summary: Fleck's recording used his father's Hoedown; Nelson Jr. settled by having Fleck pay his attorney and record father's tunes in Indianapolis.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Oh yeah. And actually I did have one I have to share with you. Bela Fleck, the great banjo player, he did an album called “Out Bound” this was several years ago. So my attorney now went to hear Bela play and they did “Hoedown.” So Aaron Copland’s “Hoedown” is owned by somebody else. So they did [scats] and then in the middle of that hoedown was my Dad’s “Hoedown.” So I said well this is a copyright infringement. So of course the attorneys start calling and two years later I get a call at midnight from Bela in Germany, he said, “Oliver we really need to kind of work this thing out.” So I said, “Well let’s do this, Bela,” I said, “you pay my attorney’s fees” — it was about three grand then so it wasn’t a huge amount but it still is money. And I said, “Come to Indianapolis, you record one or two of my Dad’s tunes, and you make sure that SONY” because he was with SONY at the time, SONY put something about my Dad on that album. So we finally got it to work. Bela — my attorney now drove down to Louisville, heard the show. They had, the Wooten Brothers were playing with them and stuff, it was great. Bela came home with me. We got home about three o’clock in the morning. My wife was watching TV waiting for me and Bela said, “Well can I sit down and watch this with you guys?” I said, “Sure.” So we had a recording session at a place called the Lodge in Indianapolis. About nine o’clock we went to the Lodge — I bought him some breakfast and we went to the Lodge. We recorded some tunes. J.J. Johnson signed — Kevin Johnson actually played on that tune because J.J. is from here and Kevin lives here now, played on that tune. I put Bela on a plane and sent him home.
Oh. Now that was a civilized way to resolve that situation.
